events.title: United Nations Charter Signed
events.description: Representatives of 50 nations signed the United Nations Charter in San Francisco at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization. The Charter came into force on October 24, 1945, after ratification by the major founding powers.
events.significance: It established the UN as the main international body for promoting peace, security, human rights, and cooperation among nations after World War II.

events.title: Berlin Airlift Begins
events.description: The United States, Britain, and France began airlifting food, fuel, and supplies to West Berlin after the Soviet Union blockaded land and water access to the city's western sectors. The operation continued for about 15 months.
events.significance: The airlift was an early Cold War confrontation that ended without direct armed conflict, demonstrated Western resolve, and contributed to the formation of NATO and the division of Germany.

events.title: St. Lawrence Seaway Opened
events.description: Queen Elizabeth II and President Dwight D. Eisenhower formally opened the St. Lawrence Seaway, a system of locks and canals connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the Great Lakes.
events.significance: The seaway allowed ocean-going vessels to reach the North American interior, boosting trade and industry in the Great Lakes region of Canada and the United States.

events.title: Human Genome Draft Announced
events.description: U.S. President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair, together with scientists Francis Collins and Craig Venter, announced the completion of a working draft of the human genome sequence.
events.significance: The announcement marked a landmark in biology and medicine, laying the groundwork for genomic medicine, personalized treatment, and modern genetic research.

events.title: Obergefell v. Hodges Decided
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that the Fourteenth Amendment requires all states to license and recognize marriages between same-sex couples.
events.significance: The decision legalized same-sex marriage nationwide in the United States and was a major milestone in the LGBTQ rights movement.
